nodes.name: Integrate by parts to bring in the D-N map
nodes.statement: Integrating by parts and using Green's formula (\ref{3.4}), we find \begin{multline} \int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M\para{\p_t^2-\Opf}w\overline{u}_1\dv \, \dd t = \int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_tu_2\overline{u}_1\dv \, \dd t\cr +\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M q(x)u_2\overline{u}_1\dv \, \dd t =-\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_{\p \M} \p_\nu w\overline{u}_1\ds \, \dd t. \end{multline} Taking (\ref{4.8}), (\ref{4.6}) into account, we deduce \begin{multline} -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_tu_2\overline{u}_1(x,t)\dv\,\dd t =\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_{\p \M}\para{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{q_2,q_2}} f_{h}(x,t)\overline{g}_h(x,t) \ds \, \dd t\cr +\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M q(x)u_2\overline{u}_1\dv \, \dd t \end{multline} where $g_h$ is given by $$ g_h(x,t)=(\theta_1\psi_{-a_1})(x,t)e^{i\varphi(x,t)/h},\quad (x,t)\in \Sigma.
nodes.statement_short: Green's formula converts the interior integral into the boundary pairing of $(\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2})f_h$ with $\overline g_h$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Expand into principal term plus remainder $\mathscr{R}_h$
nodes.statement: It follows from (\ref{4.9}), (\ref{4.6}) and (\ref{4.3}) that \begin{multline} ih^{-1}\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x) (\theta_2 \overline{\theta}_1)(x,t)(\psi_{a_2}\psi_{-a_1})( x,t)\dv\,\dd t =\cr \int_0^T\!\!\!\int_{\p \M} \overline{g}_h\para{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}}f_{h} \ds \, \dd t -ih^{-1}\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x) (\theta_2\psi_{a_2})(x,t)\overline{r}_{1,h}e^{i\varphi/h}\dv\dd t\cr +\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_t(\theta_2\psi_{a_2})(x,t)\overline{\theta}_1\psi_{a_1}(x,t)\dv\dd t +\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_t(\theta_2\psi_{a_2})(x,t)\overline{r}_{1,h}(t,x)e^{i\varphi/h}\dv\dd t\cr +\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_t r_{2,h}(\overline{\theta}_1\psi_{a_1})(x,t) e^{-i\varphi/h}\dv\dd t +\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_tr_{2,h}(x,t)\overline{r}_{1,h}(x,t)\dv\dd t\cr +\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M q(x)u_2(x,t)\overline{u}_1(x,t)\dv dt \cr = \int_0^T\!\!\!\int_{\p \M} \overline{g}_h \para{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}}f_{h} \ds \, \dd t+\mathscr{R}_h. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the two expansions and collect all terms containing $r_{1,h}$, $r_{2,h}$ or $q$ into $\mathscr{R}_h$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Bound the remainder $\mathscr{R}_h$
nodes.statement: In view of (\ref{4.7}) and (\ref{4.4}), we have \begin{equation} \abs{\mathscr{R}_h}\leq C\norm{\theta_1}_{\mathcal{V}(Q)}\norm{\theta_2}_{\mathcal{V}(Q)}.
nodes.statement_short: The remainder estimates (4.4) and (4.7) give $|\mathscr{R}_h|\le C\|\theta_1\|\|\theta_2\|$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Bound the boundary term by the trace theorem
nodes.statement_short: The trace theorem gives $Ch^{-3}\|\theta_1\|\|\theta_2\|\,\|\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}\|$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Conclude the estimate (4.2)
nodes.statement: The estimate (\ref{4.2}) follows easily from (\ref{4.10}), (\ref{4.11}) and (\ref{4.12}).\\ This completes the proof of the Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Multiply through by $h$ and combine (4.10), (4.11) and (4.12).
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Lemma 4.2 (estimate for the exponential of the ray transform of $a$)
nodes.statement: There exists $C>0$ such that for any $\Psi\in H^2 (S_y\M_{1})$, the following estimate \begin{multline} \abs{\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\para{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\I(a)(y,\xi)}-1} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)}\cr \leq C\para{h+h^{-2}\norm{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}}} \norm{\Psi}_{H^2(S_y\M_{1})}. \end{multline} holds for any $y\in\p\M_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Averages of $\exp(-\frac12\I(a)(y,\xi))-1$ against $H^2$ test functions on the inward hemisphere are controlled by $h+h^{-2}\|\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}\|$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: We take two solutions to (\ref{3.11}) of the form \begin{align*} \widetilde{\theta}_1(t,r,\xi)&=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r)\Psi(\xi), \\ \widetilde{\theta}_2(t,r,\xi)&=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r). \end{align*} Now we change variable in the left term of (\ref{4.1}), $x=\exp_{y}(r\xi)$, $r>0$ and $\xi\in S_{y}\M_1$, we have \begin{multline} \int_0^T\!\!\int_\M a(x) (\overline{\theta}_1\theta_2)(x,t)\psi_{a}(x,t) \dv \, \dd t \cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\!\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{a}(r,y,\xi)(\overline{\widetilde{\theta}}_1\widetilde{\theta}_2)( t,r,\xi) \widetilde{\psi}_{a}( t,r,\xi) \alpha^{1/2} \, \dd r \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t\cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\!\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{a}(r,y,\xi)\phi^2( t-r)\widetilde{\psi}_{a}( t,r,\xi)\Psi(\xi) \, \dd r \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t\cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\!\int_\R \widetilde{a}( t-\tau,y,\xi)\phi^2(\tau)\widetilde{\psi}_{a}( t, t-\tau,\xi)\Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t\cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\!\int_\R \widetilde{a}( t-\tau,y,\xi)\phi^2(\tau)\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{ t}\widetilde{a}(s-\tau,y,\xi)ds} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)\cr =2\int_\R\phi^2(\tau) \!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\int_0^T \frac{d}{dt}\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{ t}\widetilde{a}(s-\tau,y,\xi)ds} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)\cr =2\int_\R\phi^2(\tau) \!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\cro{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{ T}\widetilde{a}(s-\tau,y,\xi)ds}-1} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi). \end{multline} By the support properties of the function $\phi$, we get that the left-hand side term in (\ref{4.14}) reads \begin{multline*} \int_\R\phi^2(\tau) \!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\cro{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{T}\widetilde{a}(s-\tau,y,\xi)ds}-1} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)=\cr \int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\cro{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{a}(s,y,\xi)ds}-1} \Psi(\xi) \mu(y,\xi) \, \dd\omega_y(\xi). \end{multline*} Then, by (\ref{4.14}) and (\ref{4.2}) we get \begin{multline} \abs{\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\para{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\I(a)(y,\xi)}-1} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)}\cr \leq C\para{h+h^{-2}\norm{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}}} \norm{\Psi}_{H^2(S_y\M_{1})}. \end{multline} This completes the proof of the Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Choose the two amplitudes so the integrand collapses to $\phi^2$, change to polar normal coordinates, integrate the exact $t$-derivative and apply Lemma 4.1.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Choose the two amplitudes
nodes.statement: We take two solutions to (\ref{3.11}) of the form \begin{align*} \widetilde{\theta}_1(t,r,\xi)&=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r)\Psi(\xi), \\ \widetilde{\theta}_2(t,r,\xi)&=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Take $\widetilde\theta_1=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r)\Psi(\xi)$ and $\widetilde\theta_2=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r)$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Change variables to polar normal coordinates
nodes.statement: Now we change variable in the left term of (\ref{4.1}), $x=\exp_{y}(r\xi)$, $r>0$ and $\xi\in S_{y}\M_1$, we have \begin{multline} \int_0^T\!\!\int_\M a(x) (\overline{\theta}_1\theta_2)(x,t)\psi_{a}(x,t) \dv \, \dd t \cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\!\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{a}(r,y,\xi)(\overline{\widetilde{\theta}}_1\widetilde{\theta}_2)( t,r,\xi) \widetilde{\psi}_{a}( t,r,\xi) \alpha^{1/2} \, \dd r \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t\cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\!\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{a}(r,y,\xi)\phi^2( t-r)\widetilde{\psi}_{a}( t,r,\xi)\Psi(\xi) \, \dd r \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t\cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\!\int_\R \widetilde{a}( t-\tau,y,\xi)\phi^2(\tau)\widetilde{\psi}_{a}( t, t-\tau,\xi)\Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t\cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\!\int_\R \widetilde{a}( t-\tau,y,\xi)\phi^2(\tau)\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{ t}\widetilde{a}(s-\tau,y,\xi)ds} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)\cr =2\int_\R\phi^2(\tau) \!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\int_0^T \frac{d}{dt}\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{ t}\widetilde{a}(s-\tau,y,\xi)ds} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)\cr =2\int_\R\phi^2(\tau) \!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\cro{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{ T}\widetilde{a}(s-\tau,y,\xi)ds}-1} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi). \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: In $(r,\xi)$ coordinates the volume element cancels $\alpha^{-1/2}$ and the $t$-integral becomes an exact derivative.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Use the support of $\phi$
nodes.statement: By the support properties of the function $\phi$, we get that the left-hand side term in (\ref{4.14}) reads \begin{multline*} \int_\R\phi^2(\tau) \!\!\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\cro{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{T}\widetilde{a}(s-\tau,y,\xi)ds}-1} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd \tau \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)=\cr \int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\cro{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{a}(s,y,\xi)ds}-1} \Psi(\xi) \mu(y,\xi) \, \dd\omega_y(\xi). \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Support of $\phi$ replaces the upper limit $T$ by $\ell_+(y,\xi)$, producing $\I(a)$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Then, by (\ref{4.14}) and (\ref{4.2}) we get \begin{multline} \abs{\int_{S^+_{y}\M_1}\para{\exp\para{-\frac{1}{2}\I(a)(y,\xi)}-1} \Psi(\xi) \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)}\cr \leq C\para{h+h^{-2}\norm{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}}} \norm{\Psi}_{H^2(S_y\M_{1})}. \end{multline} This completes the proof of the Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the identity into the preliminary estimate (4.2).
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Poisson kernel $P(\theta,\xi)$ on $T_y\M_1$ and the mollifier $\Psi_\kappa$
nodes.statement: We define the Poisson kernel of $B(0,1)\subset T_y \M_1$, i.e., $$ P(\theta,\xi)=\frac{1-\abs{\theta}^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\theta-\xi}^n},\quad \theta\in B(0,1);\,\, \xi\in S_y\M_1. $$ For $0<\kappa<1$, we define $\Psi_\kappa: S_y\M_1\times S_y\M_1\to \R$ as \begin{align} \Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi)=P(\kappa\theta,\xi). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $P(\theta,\xi)=(1-|\theta|^2)/(\alpha_n|\theta-\xi|^n)$, and $\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi)=P(\kappa\theta,\xi)$ is an approximate identity as $\kappa\to1$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Lemma 4.3 (properties of the mollifier $\Psi_\kappa$)
nodes.statement: Let $\Psi_\kappa$ given by (\ref{4.16}), $\kappa \in (0,1)$. Then we have the following properties: \begin{equation} \displaystyle 0\leq\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi)\leq \frac{2}{\alpha_n(1-\kappa)^{n-1}},\quad \forall\, \kappa\in (0,1),\,\forall\,\xi,\theta \in S_y\M_1. \end{equation} \begin{equation} \displaystyle \int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) d\omega_y(\xi)=1,\quad \forall \kappa\in (0,1),\,\forall\,\theta \in S_y\M_1. \end{equation} \begin{equation} \int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)\leq C(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}, \quad \forall\, \kappa\in (0,1),\,\forall\,\theta \in S_y\M_1. \end{equation} \begin{equation} \norm{ \Psi_\kappa(\theta,\cdot)}_{H^2(S_y\M_1)}^2\leq \frac{C}{(1-\kappa)^{n+3}}, \quad \forall \kappa\in (0,1),\,\forall\,\theta \in S_y\M_1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\Psi_\kappa$ is positive, has unit mass, concentrates at rate $(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}$ and has $H^2$ norm $O((1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)/2})$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4 (pointwise estimate for the ray transform of $a$)
nodes.statement: Let $a_{i}\in \mathscr{A}(m_{1},\alpha)$, $q_i \in \mathscr{Q}(m_2)$, $i=1,\,2$. There exist $C>0,$ $\delta>0$, $\beta>0$ and $h_{0}>0$ such that \begin{equation} |\I(a)(y,\theta)|\leq C \Big( h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h^{\beta} \Big),\quad\forall \, (y,\theta)\in\p_+S\M_1, \end{equation} for any $h\leq h_{0}$. Here $C$ depends only on $\M$, $T$, $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: $|\I(a)(y,\theta)|\le C(h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}-\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}\|+h^\beta)$ uniformly on $\p_+S\M_1$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: Let $(y,\theta)\in\p_+S\M_1$ be a fixed and let $\Psi_\kappa$ be the positive function given by (\ref{4.16}). We extend $\I(a)$ by zero in $\p_-S\M$, then, we have \begin{multline} \Big|\exp\para{-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\theta)} -1 \Big|=\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\Big[ \exp\Big(-\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta) \Big)-1 \Big]\,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr \leq\quad \Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\Big[\exp\Big( -\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\theta) \Big) -\exp\Big(-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\xi)\Big) \Big] \,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr +\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1} \Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\Big[\exp\Big(-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\xi) \Big)-1 \Big] d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|. \end{multline} Therefore, since we have $$\begin{array}{lll} \Big| \!\exp\Big( \!-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\theta)\Big) \!-\!\exp\Big(\! -\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\xi) \! \Big) \Big|\!\!\!&\leq&\!\!\! C\Big|\displaystyle \I(a)(y,\theta)-\I(a)(y,\xi)\Big|,\cr \end{array}$$ and using the fact that $$ \Big|\displaystyle \I(a)(y,\theta)-\I(a)(y,\xi)\Big|\leq C \,|\theta-\xi|, $$ we deduce upon applying Lemma \ref{L.4.2} with $\Psi=\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\cdot)$ the following estimation \begin{multline*} \Big|\exp\Big(-\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\theta)\Big)-1 \Big|\leq \cr C\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\,|\theta-\xi|\,d\omega_y(\xi)+C\Big( h^{-2}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h \Big)\|\Psi_{\kappa}\|_{H^2(S_y\M_1)}^{2}. \end{multline*} On the other hand, by (\ref{4.20}) and (\ref{4.19}), we have the following inequality $$ \Big|\exp\Big(-\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta)\Big)-1 \Big|\leq C \,(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+C\Big( h^{-2}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h \Big)(1-\kappa)^{-(3+n)}. $$ Selecting $(1-\kappa)$ small such that $(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}=h(1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)}$, that is $(1-\kappa)=h^{2n/1+2n^2+6n}$, we find two constants $\delta>0$ and $\beta>0$ such that $$\Big| \exp \Big( -\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta) \Big)-1 \Big|\leq C \Big[ h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h^{\beta} \Big].$$ Now, using the fact that $|X|\leq e^{M}\,|e^{X}-1|$ for any $|X|\leq M$, we deduce that $$\Big| -\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta) \Big|\leq e^{M_{1}T}\Big| \exp\Big( -\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta) \Big)-1 \Big|.$$ Hence, we conclude that for all $\theta\in S_y\M_1$ and $y\in $ we have $$ \Big|\I(a)(y,\theta) \Big|\leq C \Big(h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h^{\beta}\Big). $$ The proof of Lemma \ref{L.4.4} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Mollify with the Poisson kernel: split into a modulus-of-continuity term and a term handled by Lemma 4.2, then optimise $\kappa$ against $h$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Mollify with the Poisson kernel
nodes.statement: Let $(y,\theta)\in\p_+S\M_1$ be a fixed and let $\Psi_\kappa$ be the positive function given by (\ref{4.16}). We extend $\I(a)$ by zero in $\p_-S\M$, then, we have \begin{multline} \Big|\exp\para{-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\theta)} -1 \Big|=\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\Big[ \exp\Big(-\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta) \Big)-1 \Big]\,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr \leq\quad \Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\Big[\exp\Big( -\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\theta) \Big) -\exp\Big(-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\xi)\Big) \Big] \,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr +\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1} \Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\Big[\exp\Big(-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\xi) \Big)-1 \Big] d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Use $\int\Psi_\kappa=1$ to split $|\exp(-\frac12\I(a)(y,\theta))-1|$ into two averaged terms.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 4.2 to the second term
nodes.statement: Therefore, since we have $$\begin{array}{lll} \Big| \!\exp\Big( \!-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\theta)\Big) \!-\!\exp\Big(\! -\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\xi) \! \Big) \Big|\!\!\!&\leq&\!\!\! C\Big|\displaystyle \I(a)(y,\theta)-\I(a)(y,\xi)\Big|,\cr \end{array}$$ and using the fact that $$ \Big|\displaystyle \I(a)(y,\theta)-\I(a)(y,\xi)\Big|\leq C \,|\theta-\xi|, $$ we deduce upon applying Lemma \ref{L.4.2} with $\Psi=\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\cdot)$ the following estimation \begin{multline*} \Big|\exp\Big(-\frac{1}{2}\,\I(a)(y,\theta)\Big)-1 \Big|\leq \cr C\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\,|\theta-\xi|\,d\omega_y(\xi)+C\Big( h^{-2}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h \Big)\|\Psi_{\kappa}\|_{H^2(S_y\M_1)}^{2}. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz continuity of $\exp$ and of $\I(a)$ in the direction, plus Lemma 4.2 with $\Psi=\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\cdot)$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Insert the mollifier bounds
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by (\ref{4.20}) and (\ref{4.19}), we have the following inequality $$ \Big|\exp\Big(-\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta)\Big)-1 \Big|\leq C \,(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+C\Big( h^{-2}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h \Big)(1-\kappa)^{-(3+n)}.
nodes.statement_short: Use (4.19) and (4.20) from Lemma 4.3 to make the $\kappa$-dependence explicit.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Optimise $\kappa$ against $h$
nodes.statement: Selecting $(1-\kappa)$ small such that $(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}=h(1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)}$, that is $(1-\kappa)=h^{2n/1+2n^2+6n}$, we find two constants $\delta>0$ and $\beta>0$ such that $$\Big| \exp \Big( -\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta) \Big)-1 \Big|\leq C \Big[ h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h^{\beta} \Big].$$
nodes.statement_short: Balance $(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}=h(1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)}$ to produce exponents $\delta,\beta>0$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Remove the exponential
nodes.statement: Now, using the fact that $|X|\leq e^{M}\,|e^{X}-1|$ for any $|X|\leq M$, we deduce that $$\Big| -\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta) \Big|\leq e^{M_{1}T}\Big| \exp\Big( -\frac{1}{2}\, \I(a)(y,\theta) \Big)-1 \Big|.$$ Hence, we conclude that for all $\theta\in S_y\M_1$ and $y\in $ we have $$ \Big|\I(a)(y,\theta) \Big|\leq C \Big(h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+h^{\beta}\Big). $$ The proof of Lemma \ref{L.4.4} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Use $|X|\le e^M|e^X-1|$ for bounded $X$ to pass from the exponential to $\I(a)$ itself.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Proof of the Holder stability estimate for the absorption coefficient
nodes.statement: Integrating the estimate (\ref{4.21}) over $\p_+S\M_1,$ with respect to $ \mu(y,\theta) \, \dss (y,\theta)$, then minimizing on $h$, we get \begin{equation} \|\I(a)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+\delta}}. \end{equation} With respect to the Theorem \ref{theorem}, we have \begin{equation} \|a\|_{L^2(\M)}\leq C \|\I(a)\|_{H^1(\p_+S\M_1)}. \end{equation} By interpolation inequality and (\ref{2.7}), we have \begin{align} \|\I(a)\|^2_{H^1(\p_+S\M_1)} & \leq C \|\I(a)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}\|\I(a)\|_{H^2(\p_+S\M_1)} \cr & \leq C \|\I(a)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}. \end{align} Combining with (\ref{4.24}) and (\ref{4.25}), we get $$ \|a\|_{L^2(\M)}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{s_0}, $$ where $s_0=\frac{\beta}{2(\beta+\delta)}$.\\ Moreover, let $\eta_0\in (n/2,\eta)$, by Sobolev emedding and interpolation inequality, there exists $\delta\in(0,1)$ such that \begin{align} \|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}\leq\norm{a}_{H^{\eta_0}(\M)}\leq C \|a\|^{\delta}_{L^2(\M)}\|a\|^{1-\delta}_{H^\eta(\M)}\leq C \|a\|^\delta_{L^2(\M)}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{\delta s_0}. \end{align} This completes the proof of the H\"older stability estimate of the absorption coefficient.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the pointwise bound, optimise in $h$, invert the ray transform by Theorem 2.1 and interpolate to get $\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0}\le C\|\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}-\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}\|^{\delta s_0}$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Integrate and optimise in $h$
nodes.statement: Integrating the estimate (\ref{4.21}) over $\p_+S\M_1,$ with respect to $ \mu(y,\theta) \, \dss (y,\theta)$, then minimizing on $h$, we get \begin{equation} \|\I(a)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+\delta}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Integrating over $\p_+S\M_1$ and minimising in $h$ gives an $L^2$ bound for $\I(a)$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Apply the ray transform stability estimate
nodes.statement: With respect to the Theorem \ref{theorem}, we have \begin{equation} \|a\|_{L^2(\M)}\leq C \|\I(a)\|_{H^1(\p_+S\M_1)}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Interpolate between $L^2$ and $H^2$
nodes.statement: By interpolation inequality and (\ref{2.7}), we have \begin{align} \|\I(a)\|^2_{H^1(\p_+S\M_1)} & \leq C \|\I(a)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}\|\I(a)\|_{H^2(\p_+S\M_1)} \cr & \leq C \|\I(a)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Interpolation plus boundedness of $\I$ converts the $H^1$ norm into the $L^2$ norm.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Obtain the $L^2$ stability estimate
nodes.statement: Combining with (\ref{4.24}) and (\ref{4.25}), we get $$ \|a\|_{L^2(\M)}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{s_0}, $$ where $s_0=\frac{\beta}{2(\beta+\delta)}$.
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Upgrade to a $\mathcal{C}^0$ estimate
nodes.statement: Moreover, let $\eta_0\in (n/2,\eta)$, by Sobolev emedding and interpolation inequality, there exists $\delta\in(0,1)$ such that \begin{align} \|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}\leq\norm{a}_{H^{\eta_0}(\M)}\leq C \|a\|^{\delta}_{L^2(\M)}\|a\|^{1-\delta}_{H^\eta(\M)}\leq C \|a\|^\delta_{L^2(\M)}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{\delta s_0}. \end{align} This completes the proof of the H\"older stability estimate of the absorption coefficient.
nodes.statement_short: Sobolev embedding and interpolation with the a priori $H^\eta$ bound give the $\mathcal{C}^0(\M)$ estimate (4.26).
nodes.section: 4 Stable determination of the absorption coefficient

nodes.name: Standing assumptions for the electric potential
nodes.statement: In this section, we prove a stability estimate for the electric potential $q$. We use the stability result obtained for the absorption coefficient $a$. Like in the previous section, we let $a_1,\,a_2\in\mathscr{A}(m_1,\eta)$ and $q_1,q_2\in\mathscr{Q}(m_2)$ such that $a_1=a_2$, $q_1=q_2$ near the boundary $\p\M$. We set $$ a(x)=(a_1-a_2)(x),\quad q(x)=(q_1-q_2)(x). $$ Recall that we have extended $a_{1},a_{2}$ as $W^{2,\infty}(\M_1)$ in such a way that $a=0$ and $q=0$ on $\M_{1} \setminus \M$.\\ We denote $\psi_{a_2}\in\mathcal{W}(Q)$ and $\psi_{-a_1}\in \mathcal{W}(Q)$ the solutions of (\ref{3.12}) respectively with $a=a_2$ and $a=-a_1$ given by (\ref{3.22}), and set \begin{equation} \psi_a(x,t)=\psi_{a_2}(x,t)\psi_{-a_1}(x,t). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Same normalisation as in Section 4, now used to estimate $q=q_1-q_2$ using the stability already proved for $a$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1 (preliminary estimate for the electric potential)
nodes.statement_short: The integral of $q$ against amplitude products is bounded by $C(h+h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0}+h^{-3}\|\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}\|)$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential
assumptions: for any $\theta_j\in \mathcal{V}(Q)$, $j=1,2$, satisfying the transport equation (\ref{3.11})

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement_short: Re-read identity (4.10) as an identity for $q$, bound the new remainder using the already-established control on $a$, and remove the weight $\psi_a$ since $|1-\psi_a|\le C\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}}$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Rewrite identity (4.10) for $q$
nodes.statement: From the equality (\ref{4.10}) and the expressions (\ref{4.6}) and (\ref{4.3}), it follows that \begin{multline} \int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M q(x)(\theta_2\overline{\theta}_1)(x,t)\psi_{a}(x,t)\,\dv dt = - \int_0^T\!\!\!\int_{\p \M} \overline{g}_h\para{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}}f_{h} \ds \, \dd t \cr +ih^{-1}\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x) (\theta_2 \overline{\theta}_1)(x,t)(\psi_{a_2}\psi_{-a_1})( x,t)\dv\,\dd t +ih^{-1}\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x) (\theta_2\psi_{a_2})(x,t))\overline{r}_{1,h}e^{i\varphi/h}\dv\dd t\cr -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_t(\theta_2\psi_{a_2})(x,t)(\overline{\theta}_1\psi_{a_1})(x,t)\dv\dd t -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_t(\theta_2\psi_{a_2})(x,t)\overline{r}_{1,h}(x,t)e^{i\varphi/h}\dv\dd t\cr -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_t r_{2,h}(\overline{\theta}_1\psi_{a_1})(x,t) e^{-i\varphi/h}\dv\dd t -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M a(x)\p_tr_{2,h}(x,t)\overline{r}_{1,h}(x,t)\dv\dd t\cr -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M q(x)(\overline{\theta}_1\psi_{-a_1})(x,t)r_{2,h}(x,t)e^{-i\varphi/h}\dv\dd t -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M q(x)(\theta_2\psi_{a_2})(x,t)\overline{r}_{1,h}(x,t)e^{i\varphi/h}\dv\dd t\cr -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M q(x)(r_{2,h}\overline{r}_{1,h})(x,t)\dv\dd t . \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Move every $a$-term and every remainder term to the right-hand side.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Bound the remainder $\mathscr{R}'_h$
nodes.statement: We set $$\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_\M q(x)(\theta_2\overline{\theta}_1)(x,t)\psi_{a}(x,t)\,\dv dt = -\int_0^T\!\!\!\int_{\p \M} \overline{g}_h\para{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}}f_{h} \ds \, \dd t +\mathscr{R}'_h.$$ In view of (\ref{4.7}) and (\ref{4.4}), we have \begin{equation} \abs{\mathscr{R}'_h}\leq C\para{h+h^{-1} \|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}}\norm{\theta_1}_{\mathcal{V}(Q)}\norm{\theta_2}_{\mathcal{V}(Q)}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $|\mathscr{R}'_h|\le C(h+h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0})\|\theta_1\|\|\theta_2\|$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Bound the boundary term by the trace theorem
nodes.statement_short: Again $Ch^{-3}\|\theta_1\|\|\theta_2\|\,\|\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}\|$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Remove the weight $\psi_a$
nodes.statement_short: Since $|1-\psi_a|\le C\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}(\M)}$, the unweighted integral differs by a controlled term.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2 (estimate for the ray transform of $q$)
nodes.statement_short: Averages of $\I q(y,\xi)$ against $H^2$ test functions are bounded by $C(h+h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0}+h^{-3}\|\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}-\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}\|)$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: As in Lemma \ref{L.4.2}, we take two solutions to (\ref{3.11}) of the form \begin{align*} \widetilde{\theta}_1(t,r,\xi)&=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r)\Psi(\xi), \\ \widetilde{\theta}_2(t,r,\xi)&=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r). \end{align*} We change variable in the left term of (\ref{5.2}), $x=\exp_{y}(r\xi)$, $r>0$ and $\xi\in S_{y}\M_1$. We have \begin{multline} \int_0^T\!\!\int_\M q(x) (\overline{\theta}_1\theta_2)(x,t) \dv \, \dd t \cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S_{y}\M_1}\!\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{q}(r,y,\xi)(\overline{\widetilde{\theta}}_1\widetilde{\theta}_2)( t,r,\xi) \alpha^{1/2} \, \dd r \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t\cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S_{y}\M_1}\!\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{q}(r,y,\xi)\phi^2( t-r)\Psi(\xi) \, \dd r \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t. \end{multline} By support properties of the function $\phi$, we get $$\int_0^T\!\!\int_\M q(x) (\overline{\theta}_1\theta_2)(x,t) \dv \, \dd t=\bigg(\int_\R\phi^2(t)\,dt \bigg) \!\!\int_{S_{y}\M_1}\I q(y,\xi) \Psi(\xi) \, \, \dd\omega_y(\xi). $$ Then, by (\ref{5.2}), we get \begin{equation} \bigg|\int_{S_{y}\M_1}\I q(y,\xi) \Psi(\xi) \, \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)\bigg| \leq C\para{h+h^{-1} \|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h^{-3}\norm{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1} -\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}} } \norm{\Psi}_{H^2(S^+_y\M_{1})}. \end{equation} This compete the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Same amplitude choice and change of variables as in Lemma 4.2; the $t$-integration now produces $\I q$ directly.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Choose the two amplitudes
nodes.statement: As in Lemma \ref{L.4.2}, we take two solutions to (\ref{3.11}) of the form \begin{align*} \widetilde{\theta}_1(t,r,\xi)&=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r)\Psi(\xi), \\ \widetilde{\theta}_2(t,r,\xi)&=\alpha^{-1/4}\phi(t-r). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reuse the amplitudes $\widetilde\theta_1,\widetilde\theta_2$ of Lemma 4.2.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Change variables to polar normal coordinates
nodes.statement: We change variable in the left term of (\ref{5.2}), $x=\exp_{y}(r\xi)$, $r>0$ and $\xi\in S_{y}\M_1$. We have \begin{multline} \int_0^T\!\!\int_\M q(x) (\overline{\theta}_1\theta_2)(x,t) \dv \, \dd t \cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S_{y}\M_1}\!\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{q}(r,y,\xi)(\overline{\widetilde{\theta}}_1\widetilde{\theta}_2)( t,r,\xi) \alpha^{1/2} \, \dd r \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t\cr =\int_0^T\!\!\int_{S_{y}\M_1}\!\int_0^{\ell_+(y,\xi)}\widetilde{q}(r,y,\xi)\phi^2( t-r)\Psi(\xi) \, \dd r \, \dd\omega_y(\xi) \, \dd t. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: The volume element cancels $\alpha^{-1/2}$, leaving $\int\widetilde q\,\phi^2(t-r)\Psi$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Use the support of $\phi$ and apply Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: By support properties of the function $\phi$, we get $$\int_0^T\!\!\int_\M q(x) (\overline{\theta}_1\theta_2)(x,t) \dv \, \dd t=\bigg(\int_\R\phi^2(t)\,dt \bigg) \!\!\int_{S_{y}\M_1}\I q(y,\xi) \Psi(\xi) \, \, \dd\omega_y(\xi). $$ Then, by (\ref{5.2}), we get \begin{equation} \bigg|\int_{S_{y}\M_1}\I q(y,\xi) \Psi(\xi) \, \, \dd\omega_y(\xi)\bigg| \leq C\para{h+h^{-1} \|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h^{-3}\norm{\Lambda_{a_1,q_1} -\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}} } \norm{\Psi}_{H^2(S^+_y\M_{1})}. \end{equation} This compete the proof.
nodes.statement_short: The $t$-integral factorises as $\int\phi^2$ times $\int\I q\,\Psi$; then apply (5.2).
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Lemma 5.3 (pointwise estimate for the ray transform of $q$)
nodes.statement: Let $a_{i}\in \mathscr{A}(m_1,\alpha)$, $q_i\in \mathscr{Q}(m_2)$, $i=1,\,2$. There exist $C>0,$ $\delta>0$, $\beta>0$ and $h_{0}>0$ such that \begin{equation} |\I(q)(y,\theta)|\leq C \Big( h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},b_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1}}\|+ h^{-\delta}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h^{\beta} \Big),\quad\forall \, (y,\theta)\in\p_+S\M_1, \end{equation} for any $h\leq h_{0}$. Here $C$ depends only on $\M$, $T$, $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: $|\I(q)(y,\theta)|\le C(h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda-\Lambda\|+h^{-\delta}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0}+h^\beta)$ uniformly on $\p_+S\M_1$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement: We fix $(y,\theta)\in\p_+S\M$ and let the positive function $\Psi_\kappa$ given by (\ref{5.10}), we have \begin{multline} \Big|\I(q)(y,\theta)\Big|=\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\I(q)(y,\theta)\,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr \leq\quad \Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi) \Big(\I(q)(y,\theta) -\I(q)(y,\xi)\Big) \,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr +\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1} \Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\I(q)(y,\xi) d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|. \end{multline} Since we have $$ \Big|\displaystyle \I(q)(y,\theta)-\I(q)(y,\xi)\Big|\leq C \,|\theta-\xi|, $$ then we deduce upon applying Lemma \ref{L.5.2} with $\Psi=\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\cdot)$ that we have the following estimation \begin{multline*} \Big|\I(q)(y,\theta)\Big|\leq C\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\,|\theta-\xi|\,d\omega_y(\xi)\cr +C\Big(h+ h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h^{-3}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\| \Big)\|\Psi_{\kappa}\|_{H^2(S_y\M_1)}^{2}. \end{multline*} On the other hand, by (\ref{4.20}) and (\ref{4.19}), we obtain $$ \Big|\I(q)(y,\theta)\Big|\leq C \,(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+C\Big( h^{-3}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+ h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h \Big)(1-\kappa)^{-(3+n)}. $$ Take $(1-\kappa)$ small such that $(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}=h(1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)}$, that is $(1-\kappa)=h^{2n/1+2n^2+6n}$, we find two constants $\delta>0$ and $\beta>0$ such that $$\Big| \I(q)(y,\theta) \Big|\leq C \Big[ h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+ h^{-\delta}\norm{a}_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h^{\beta} \Big].$$ The proof of Lemma \ref{L.5.3} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Same Poisson-kernel mollification as in Lemma 4.4, now applied directly to $\I(q)$ and using Lemma 5.2.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Mollify with the Poisson kernel
nodes.statement: We fix $(y,\theta)\in\p_+S\M$ and let the positive function $\Psi_\kappa$ given by (\ref{5.10}), we have \begin{multline} \Big|\I(q)(y,\theta)\Big|=\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\I(q)(y,\theta)\,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr \leq\quad \Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi) \Big(\I(q)(y,\theta) -\I(q)(y,\xi)\Big) \,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr +\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\M_1} \Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\I(q)(y,\xi) d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Split $|\I(q)(y,\theta)|$ into a modulus-of-continuity term and an averaged term.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: Since we have $$ \Big|\displaystyle \I(q)(y,\theta)-\I(q)(y,\xi)\Big|\leq C \,|\theta-\xi|, $$ then we deduce upon applying Lemma \ref{L.5.2} with $\Psi=\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\cdot)$ that we have the following estimation \begin{multline*} \Big|\I(q)(y,\theta)\Big|\leq C\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\,|\theta-\xi|\,d\omega_y(\xi)\cr +C\Big(h+ h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h^{-3}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\| \Big)\|\Psi_{\kappa}\|_{H^2(S_y\M_1)}^{2}. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Lipschitz continuity of $\I(q)$ in the direction and Lemma 5.2 with $\Psi=\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\cdot)$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Insert the mollifier bounds
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by (\ref{4.20}) and (\ref{4.19}), we obtain $$ \Big|\I(q)(y,\theta)\Big|\leq C \,(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+C\Big( h^{-3}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+ h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h \Big)(1-\kappa)^{-(3+n)}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply (4.19) and (4.20) of Lemma 4.3.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Optimise $\kappa$ against $h$
nodes.statement: Take $(1-\kappa)$ small such that $(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}=h(1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)}$, that is $(1-\kappa)=h^{2n/1+2n^2+6n}$, we find two constants $\delta>0$ and $\beta>0$ such that $$\Big| \I(q)(y,\theta) \Big|\leq C \Big[ h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+ h^{-\delta}\norm{a}_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)}+h^{\beta} \Big].$$ The proof of Lemma \ref{L.5.3} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Balance $(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}=h(1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)}$ to obtain $\delta,\beta>0$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Proof of the stability estimate for the electric potential
nodes.statement: Integrating the estimate (\ref{5.11}) over $\p_+S\M_1,$ with respect to $ \mu(y,\theta) \, \dss (y,\theta)$, then minimizing on $h$, we get \begin{equation} \|\I(q)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}\leq C ( \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)})^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+\delta}}. \end{equation} By interpolation inequality, we get \begin{align} \norm{\I(q)}^2_{H^1(\p_+S\M_1)} & \leq C \|\I(q)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}\|\I(q)\|_{H^2(\p_+S\M_1)} \cr & \leq C \|\I(q)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}. \end{align} From the Theorem \ref{theorem}, it follows that \begin{equation} \|q\|_{L^2(\M)}\leq C ( \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)})^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+\delta}}. \end{equation} Using the estimate (\ref{4.26}), we conclude that $$ \|q\|_{L^2(\M)}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{s_1}, $$ where $s_1 \in (0,1)$. This completes the proof of the Theorem \ref{Th2}.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate, optimise in $h$, invert the ray transform by Theorem 2.1, then eliminate $\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0}$ with estimate (4.26) to finish Theorem 1.4.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Integrate and optimise in $h$
nodes.statement: Integrating the estimate (\ref{5.11}) over $\p_+S\M_1,$ with respect to $ \mu(y,\theta) \, \dss (y,\theta)$, then minimizing on $h$, we get \begin{equation} \|\I(q)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}\leq C ( \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)})^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+\delta}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Gives an $L^2(\p_+S\M_1)$ bound for $\I(q)$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Interpolate the $H^1$ norm
nodes.statement: By interpolation inequality, we get \begin{align} \norm{\I(q)}^2_{H^1(\p_+S\M_1)} & \leq C \|\I(q)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}\|\I(q)\|_{H^2(\p_+S\M_1)} \cr & \leq C \|\I(q)\|_{L^2(\p_+S\M_1)}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Apply the ray transform stability estimate
nodes.statement: From the Theorem \ref{theorem}, it follows that \begin{equation} \|q\|_{L^2(\M)}\leq C ( \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\M)})^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+\delta}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 2.1 turns the bound on $\I(q)$ into a bound on $\|q\|_{L^2(\M)}$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Eliminate $\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0}$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Using the estimate (\ref{4.26}), we conclude that $$ \|q\|_{L^2(\M)}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{s_1}, $$ where $s_1 \in (0,1)$. This completes the proof of the Theorem \ref{Th2}.
nodes.statement_short: Substituting the already-proved stability for $a$ gives $\|q\|_{L^2}\le C\|\Lambda_{a_2,q_2}-\Lambda_{a_1,q_1}\|^{s_1}$.
nodes.section: 5 Stable determination of the electric potential

nodes.name: Euclidean Poisson kernel $P_0$
nodes.statement: Let $P_0$ the Poisson kernel for the Euclidian unit ball $B_0(0,1)\subset\R^n$ i.e., $$ P_0(\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi})=\frac{1-\abs{\hat{\theta}}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\hat{\theta}-\hat{\xi}}_0^n},\quad \hat{\theta}\in B_0(0,1);\,\, \hat{\xi}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$ where $\abs{\cdot}_0$ is the Euclidian norm of $\R^n$.
nodes.section: Appendix A Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.definiendum: the Poisson kernel for the Euclidian unit ball $B_0(0,1)\subset\R^n$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: Let $P_0$ the Poisson kernel for the Euclidian unit ball $B_0(0,1)\subset\R^n$ i.e., $$ P_0(\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi})=\frac{1-\abs{\hat{\theta}}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\hat{\theta}-\hat{\xi}}_0^n},\quad \hat{\theta}\in B_0(0,1);\,\, \hat{\xi}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$ where $\abs{\cdot}_0$ is the Euclidian norm of $\R^n$. From the well known properties of $P_0$, we have $$ \int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}P_0(\kappa\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi}) d\omega_0(\hat{\xi})=1, \quad\textrm{for all}\, \kappa\in (0,1),\,\, \hat{\theta}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$ Let $\gamma=\sqrt{\g}:=(\gamma_{ij})$ be definite symetric positive matrix such that $\gamma^2=(g_{ij})$, then we get $$ P(\theta,\xi)=\frac{1-\abs{\gamma^{-1}\theta}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\gamma^{-1}\theta-\gamma^{-1}\xi}_0^n},\quad \theta,\xi\in S_y\M. $$ we deduce from the change of variable $\hat{\xi}=\gamma^{-1}\xi$ \begin{eqnarray} \int_{S_y\M_1}P(\kappa\theta,\xi)d\omega_y(\xi)&=&\int_{S_y\M_1}P_0(\kappa\gamma^{-1}\theta,\gamma^{-1}\xi)d\omega_y(\xi)\cr &=&\frac{1}{\det\gamma}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}P_0(\kappa\gamma^{-1}\theta,\hat{\xi})(\det\gamma) d\omega_0(\hat{\xi})=1 \end{eqnarray} This complete the proof of (\ref{4.18}). Let now $$ V_\theta=\set{\xi\in S_y\M_1,\,\,\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}\leq (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}}. $$ \begin{multline} \int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)\leq\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr \int_{V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+\int_{S_y\M_1\backslash V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+4(1-\kappa)^{1/2}+(1-\kappa)\leq C(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}, \end{multline} and then we get (\ref{4.19}).\\ By a simple computation, we have $$ \abs{\nabla_\xi^k P(\kappa\theta,\xi)}\leq C\frac{1-\kappa^2}{\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}^{n+k}},\quad k=1,2, $$ we deduce that \begin{equation} \norm{ \Psi_\kappa(\theta,\cdot)}^2_{H^2(S_y\M_1)} \leq C\frac{1-\kappa^2}{(1-\kappa)^{n+4}}\int_{S_y\M_1}\frac{1-\kappa^2}{\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}^n} d\omega_y(\xi)\leq \frac{C}{(1-\kappa)^{n+3}}. \end{equation} This complete the proof of (\ref{4.20}).
nodes.statement_short: Transfer the Euclidean Poisson kernel by the change of variable $\hat\xi=\gamma^{-1}\xi$ to get unit mass, then split the concentration integral near and far from $\kappa\theta$ and differentiate the kernel for the $H^2$ bound.
nodes.section: Appendix A Proof of Lemma 4.3

nodes.name: Unit mass of $\Psi_\kappa$
nodes.statement: Let $P_0$ the Poisson kernel for the Euclidian unit ball $B_0(0,1)\subset\R^n$ i.e., $$ P_0(\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi})=\frac{1-\abs{\hat{\theta}}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\hat{\theta}-\hat{\xi}}_0^n},\quad \hat{\theta}\in B_0(0,1);\,\, \hat{\xi}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$ where $\abs{\cdot}_0$ is the Euclidian norm of $\R^n$. From the well known properties of $P_0$, we have $$ \int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}P_0(\kappa\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi}) d\omega_0(\hat{\xi})=1, \quad\textrm{for all}\, \kappa\in (0,1),\,\, \hat{\theta}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$ Let $\gamma=\sqrt{\g}:=(\gamma_{ij})$ be definite symetric positive matrix such that $\gamma^2=(g_{ij})$, then we get $$ P(\theta,\xi)=\frac{1-\abs{\gamma^{-1}\theta}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\gamma^{-1}\theta-\gamma^{-1}\xi}_0^n},\quad \theta,\xi\in S_y\M. $$ we deduce from the change of variable $\hat{\xi}=\gamma^{-1}\xi$ \begin{eqnarray} \int_{S_y\M_1}P(\kappa\theta,\xi)d\omega_y(\xi)&=&\int_{S_y\M_1}P_0(\kappa\gamma^{-1}\theta,\gamma^{-1}\xi)d\omega_y(\xi)\cr &=&\frac{1}{\det\gamma}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}P_0(\kappa\gamma^{-1}\theta,\hat{\xi})(\det\gamma) d\omega_0(\hat{\xi})=1 \end{eqnarray} This complete the proof of (\ref{4.18}).
nodes.statement_short: Change variables by $\gamma=\sqrt{\g}$ to reduce to the Euclidean kernel, whose mass is $1$.

nodes.name: Concentration estimate
nodes.statement: Let now $$ V_\theta=\set{\xi\in S_y\M_1,\,\,\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}\leq (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}}. $$ \begin{multline} \int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)\leq\int_{S_y\M_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr \int_{V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+\int_{S_y\M_1\backslash V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+4(1-\kappa)^{1/2}+(1-\kappa)\leq C(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}, \end{multline} and then we get (\ref{4.19}).
nodes.statement_short: Split the integral over $V_\theta$ and its complement to get the $C(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}$ bound.

nodes.name: $H^2$ bound for $\Psi_\kappa$
nodes.statement: By a simple computation, we have $$ \abs{\nabla_\xi^k P(\kappa\theta,\xi)}\leq C\frac{1-\kappa^2}{\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}^{n+k}},\quad k=1,2, $$ we deduce that \begin{equation} \norm{ \Psi_\kappa(\theta,\cdot)}^2_{H^2(S_y\M_1)} \leq C\frac{1-\kappa^2}{(1-\kappa)^{n+4}}\int_{S_y\M_1}\frac{1-\kappa^2}{\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}^n} d\omega_y(\xi)\leq \frac{C}{(1-\kappa)^{n+3}}. \end{equation} This complete the proof of (\ref{4.20}).
nodes.statement_short: Differentiating the kernel twice gives $\|\Psi_\kappa\|^2_{H^2}\le C(1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)}$.
